reasoning:
The US economy mathematically registers in the Recovery phase as of August 7, 2026, supported by a Composite Growth Z-score of +0.216 and a Composite Inflation Z-score of -0.692. Following July's anomalous counterclockwise shift, the investment clock has stabilized into a clockwise trajectory, moving to 287.3 degrees. Real-economy growth momentum has accelerated dramatically, evidenced by the Atlanta Fed GDPNow Q3 forecast surging to 5.8%, ISM Manufacturing PMI reaching 55.6 (a 50-month high), initial jobless claims dropping to 199k, and unemployment easing to 4.1%.

However, a profound structural divergence has emerged within the inflation composite. While consumer inflation metrics show benign disinflation (Core CPI at 1.93% YoY and annualized CPI MoM at -0.20%), wholesale producer inflation has accelerated to 5.07% YoY (PPI Final Demand). This widening 3.14% PPI-CPI spread highlights severe wholesale pipeline cost pressures driven by industrial commodities, AI hardware capex, and energy prices ($90 Brent crude), which corporate profit margins must absorb until pass-through occurs.

Monetary policy under Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh adds further structural tension. The July FOMC decision to hold rates at 3.50%-3.75% featured a historic 9-3 hawkish dissent, with three regional presidents favoring an immediate rate hike. Coupled with Warsh's elimination of forward guidance, long-end Treasury yields have bear-steepened (10Y at 4.75%, 30Y at 5.20%). While quantitative indicators place the economy squarely in Recovery, the latent pass-through of 5.07% PPI into consumer prices makes this phase temporary, setting up a clockwise transition toward Overheat by late Q4.
outlook: Over the next 3-6 months, the economy carries a 60% probability of transitioning clockwise into the Overheat phase as Q3 GDP growth (projected at 5.8%) and 5.07% PPI wholesale inflation pass into consumer prices, lifting the Composite Inflation Z-score back above zero. A secondary scenario (30% probability) maintains the Recovery phase if AI productivity gains absorb producer costs. Tail-risk (10% probability) involves a leap into Stagflation if geopolitical energy spikes coincide with credit tightening. Key indicators to track include the PPI-CPI spread, 30-year Treasury yields, and corporate credit default spreads.
